newsitem.title: ITALY: "Euro" coins weigh on Europe's mints.
newsitem.headline: "Euro" coins weigh on Europe's mints.

text.p: A mountain of 46 billion coins weighing 300,000 tonnes will go out of circulation in 2002 if all 15 countries of the European Union join a planned single currency, Italy's mint said on Wednesday.
It published the hefty statistics on the "Euro" after officials of national mints from the 15 EU states met in Rome to discuss some of the practical implications of monetary union.
Leading makers and distributors of slot machines, which will have to be changed to suit the single currency, also attended the two-day meeting.

Economic and monetary union is due to take effect on January 1, 1999 for those EU states which meet strict economic criteria but the single currency itself will not enter public circulation until January 1, 2002.
The statement said countries would have to recall "46 billion coins weighing about 300,000 tonnes".
Minting the "Euro" and its various units would cost some four trillion lire ($2.6 billion) while the metal in the coins taken out of circulation would be worth about 1,600 billion lire, it said.
EU leaders have agreed that the Euro should show a Europe-wide design on one face and a national design on the other.
The statement said each of the 15 mints had been asked to come up with three proposed designs for the "common face" by next February. A jury would then select the winning entry by April 1997.
